headline: Measuring evidential weight of variant predictors and MAVE assays in classification
label: Variant Effect Evidence Calibration
summary: Clinical variant interpretation rules and predictor-based evidence are now being tested empirically rather than assumed, with MAVE data as the reference.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the empirical calibration of functional and computational evidence used in ACMG/AMP clinical variant classification. One item proposes mean evidence strength (MES), which scores the ACMG/AMP calibrated clinical evidence yield of missense variant effect predictors and MAVE datasets. A second analyzes MAVE functional scores across 39 genes to test whether the intra-residue missense evidence assumed by the PM5 criterion is supported, and proposes refined cut-offs. A third item benchmarks gpt-4o-mini and o4-mini on ClinGen-based variant functional evidence screening and extraction, presenting AcmGENTIC as an end-to-end pipeline. What is new is a shift from assuming evidential weight to measuring it: MES quantifies what a predictor or assay contributes to classification, while the PM5 analysis examines the basis of one specific rule. The LLM item addresses the upstream step of mining functional evidence from literature rather than its calibration.
